listen: Good morning. This is The Daily Brief for Friday, November 13. Our top story is the global Microsoft outage. Microsoft says the outage was not caused by a cyber-security incident. But efforts to fix the issues have so far been largely unsuccessful. Other coverage says services including Teams, Outlook and the Copilot AI software have been affected by connectivity problems. If your workday depends on those tools, plan accordingly. Now the front page. Jensen Huang quit as head of Nvidia on Thursday after revelations of alleged extramarital affairs. He has now been summoned to testify before Congress about an affair with an alleged Chinese spy. For Claude builders, the Claude Platform release notes from November twelfth announce self-hosted Claude Managed Agents. You can run the whole Managed Agents service on your own infrastructure and store agents, sessions and session history there. In baseball, the Braves and free agent reliever Evan Phillips agreed to a three-year, thirty-five million dollar contract. Phillips appeared in thirty-one games for the Dodgers last season. In Georgia, House Democrats nominated Representative Carolyn Hugley of Columbus as speaker. She would be the first Black person to lead the chamber. Now the sections. In tech, Anthropic is committing a portion of its shares to a new Public Benefit Fund. Anthropic is also expanding its partnership with the General Services Administration to bring Claude to all levels of government. And Simon Willison released llm-gemini zero point three seven, adding Google's Gemini 4 Hydrogen. In politics, The Lever reports Senator Josh Hawley has joined the opposition to data centers. It also reports that twenty-one Senate Democrats advanced a lame-duck permitting bill. And President Trump says there is no need for an Iran deal, and is directing Vice President Vance to focus on fraud in Democratic-led states. In world news, U.S. envoys met Russia's president and say more talks are likely, perhaps with European participation. NPR reports the president's options for ending the war in Iran are narrowing. And the FBI says North Korean hackers used fake video calls in a four hundred million dollar crypto hack. In sports, the NBA suspended Rockets guard Marcus Smart three games for a punch thrown at Warriors center Charles Bassey. The 49ers are treating Sunday's game against the Cowboys as a major test. And a boxing match between Alistair Overeem and Jimi Manuwa was added to the December twenty-fourth card. In Atlanta, two Westside developments are set to break ground on the same day this month. Georgia climbed nine spots in the Bicycle Friendly States ranking. And a letter writer questions demand for the Beltline-backed autonomous pod test. In architecture, the Archeform add-on brings BIM to SketchUp. SketchUp 2027 improves Revit interoperability. And G2 Digital launched a four-GPU server for firms. In science, Europe's Hera spacecraft is beginning its study of the asteroid Didymos. NASA reports a global rebound for mangroves. And the U.S. has proposed allowing commercial fishing in part of a Pacific marine reserve. That is the brief. Have a good day.

lead.title: What we know about the global Microsoft outage
lead.note: Microsoft is dealing with a global outage, and efforts to fix it have so far been largely unsuccessful. The company has said the outage was not caused by a cyber-security incident. That statement rules out one explanation, but the summary does not say what did go wrong. Related coverage describes services including Teams, Outlook and the Copilot AI software as affected by what Microsoft calls connectivity problems. For anyone who relies on email, chat and cloud tools to run a working day, a failure of this size is a reminder of how much depends on a small number of providers. The problem was still unresolved at the time of the latest reports, so the details may change as Microsoft continues its repairs. Check your own tools before you plan a day around them.
